newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end steady to down on USDA data.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end steady to down on USDA data.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed steady to lower on Wednesday as the USDA's November crop production report, released overnight, discouraged local investors, traders said.
Prices were unchanged to 130 yen lower, with the benchmark November 1997 contract steady at 14,210. Daily volume was 41,858 lots.

The USDA said on Tuesday the 1996 U.S. corn crop would total 9.265 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 9.149 billion. That tally was well above the October outlook for 9.012 billion.
The bearish USDA report offset the yen's fall against the dollar, traders said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.68-1/2 per bushel at 0850 GMT, against $2.68 at Tuesday's close.
The spot November contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $6.90 at 0850 GMT, against $6.88-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
